hints: In the lift’s frame, what is the effective gravity? Then it is an ordinary projectile.
worded:
1. In the frame of a lift accelerating up at 2 m/s², every free body seems to have a downward acceleration g + a = 12 m/s².

2. Relative to the lift the bullet leaves at 10 m/s at 30°, so its vertical component is 5 m/s.

3. Time of flight (back to the floor level of the gun) = 2 × 5/12 = 5/6 s. (C)

4. Check: in a lift at rest it would be 1 s (option A); the upward acceleration of the lift shortens it.
mistakes: An upward-accelerating lift increases the effective g (to g + a), not decreases it.
The lift’s velocity is irrelevant; only its acceleration matters.
